findings.element: [data-app="timeline"] .b-measure[data-across="true"] .b-item[data-lead="true"] .b-tick — src/across.css:169 overrides only the base .b-tick to left:0; the lead override at src/timeline.css:710 (left:-24px) and the [data-medium="sheet"|"full"] override at src/timeline.css:1829 (left:-28px) still win
findings.problem: In every across configuration the nearest moment's mark sits 28px to the LEFT of its own date. Measured on timeline.owner-flight: the day-16 item box is at x=524.5 and its tick centre is at 496.5 (computed left:-28px); every other tick's centre equals its item x to 0.1px. Reproduces identically at 1920/1440/1280/1024 and at 768 with &layout=across, on both paper and ink. At 1920 the scale is 20.28px/day, so the accent mark reads 1.4 days early; at 768-across the scale is 5.92px/day, so it reads 4.7 days early. It is also 24px clear of the foot of its own leader stem (.b-item::after starts at left:0), so the one filled indigo dot on the measure does not touch the line that claims it, and on a surface whose whole thesis is that position is the quantity, the single accented object is the only one that lies.
findings.fix: Add to src/across.css immediately after the .b-tick block at line 169-173: `[data-app="timeline"] .b-measure[data-across="true"] .b-item[data-lead="true"] .b-tick { left: 0; top: var(--rule-y); }`. Six compound units beats both the 4-unit rule at timeline.css:710 and the 5-unit [data-medium] rule at timeline.css:1829, so no !important and no edit to the down measure is needed. Then assert it in interaction-check.mjs: for every .b-item in an across measure, |tick centre - item left| <= 1px.
